text:
Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Increased request latency and reduced throughput observed for inference-prod us-west cluster. 99th latency up from 250ms -> 1.8s, sustained drop in requests/sec across routes. Auto-escalation to oncall. incident_id=INC-2026-042

Alex P: seeing this now, paging Sara (next oncall) and runtime. tagging @Jordan M. I’m on initial triage.

Alex P: quick checks — no deploys in last 30m per deploy-bot, no config rollouts. metrics: sustained queueing on gpu-pool-3, RX/TX normal.

Sara K: on it, joining. what’s the customer impact? any major customers seeing 5xxs or timeouts?

Marta L: CS monitoring flags 3 customers with elevated 504s on streaming endpoints, small batch jobs failing to start. Not widespread 5xxs but elevated client retries. filing customer list to #customer-notifications.

Jordan M: digging into runtime logs. initial hypothesis: KV cache eviction storms causing long first-token latencies and pipeline stalls when we cross sequence-size distribution boundary. Saw repeated "cache-miss and refill" messages from runtime v2.4. Command I'm running: `rctl tail runtime-gpu-3 --filter cache-miss --since 15m`

Jordan M: also seeing increased GC-like pauses in the memory_metrics: GPU memory churn spikes correlated with long tokens. Might be a quantized model variant falling back to slower kernel.

Alex P: mitigation options — (A) reduce max_batch_size for affected pool, (B) enable fallback to smaller model variant earlier, (C) scale pool up by +2 replicas. Which is fastest to reduce p99?

Jordan M: fastest is (A) + (B). I can flip batch size to 8 -> 4 and lower routing weight to smaller variant. Scaling will take ~6-8 minutes to warm.

Alex P: go for A+B now. Jordan, can you post the config changes you’ll apply so I can put them in the status update draft?

Jordan M: patch snippet: ```yaml
- pool: gpu-pool-3
  max_batch_size: 4
  routing_policy:
    - model: redwood-model-v1-quant
      weight: 30
    - model: redwood-model-v1-small
      weight: 70
``` Applying via infra-run: `infractl apply --path /configs/production/pools/gpu-pool-3.yaml`

Jordan M: applying now. Expect changes to propagate in ~45-90s per worker as agent restarts streams.

OpsBot: INCIDENT INC-2026-042: Runbook step 1 executed by Jordan M — reduced max_batch_size for gpu-pool-3.

Alex P: drafting status page and customer note. Draft status: "We are investigating increased latency for inference calls in US-West. We have applied routing and batching mitigations to reduce latency. Some customers may experience degraded throughput or transient streaming interruptions. Estimated recovery within 30-60 minutes. Updates every 15 minutes." Thoughts?

CS Rep: please add customer-facing bullet: "If you rely on high-throughput batch workloads, expect lower throughput during mitigation window; best-effort retries are recommended." Also include link to status page and support contact.

Sara K: also add internal severity: Sev2 (performance impact to multiple customers) and page SRE for scaling if mitigations don't reduce p99 within 20 minutes.

Alex P: updated status page message and pushed to status page: `https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INC-2026-042` (draft). Sending customer-notifications list now.

Marta L: customer-notifications sent to affected list (IDs masked). Some replies asking for ETA — I’ll forward to this thread.

Jordan M: seeing immediate p99 improvement from 1.8s -> 650ms after batch change and routing shift. throughput down ~15% but stable. continuing to monitor.

Alex P: nice. leaving note for scaling: let’s prepare scaling command if needed. `kubectl -n inference scale sts gpu-pool-3 --replicas=6` — require approval from infra lead to hit capacity.

OpsBot: ALERT: cpu usage on control-plane rising; adding infra lead to participants.

Sara K: monitoring windows: if p99 < 800ms for 10m, we consider mitigation successful and transition to monitoring mode. Otherwise, escalate to scaling. Current timebox: 20m.

Jordan M: logs look quieter, no more eviction storms in last 3m. Keeping routing weights in place for another 20m, then we can slowly ramp back to normal if stable.

Alex P: preparing post-incident customer update template. Draft: "Update: Mitigation applied — changed batching and routing to reduce latency. Throughput reduced temporarily. We are monitoring and will post another update within 1 hour or sooner if the situation changes. If you see continued errors, contact support@redwood.com with INC-2026-042." Approve?

CS Rep: looks good. send now.

Marta L: sent customer update (masked). A couple customers acknowledged, one asked for a follow-up call — scheduling now.

Sara K: 20m check-in — p99 holding ~720ms, throughput stable. marking as "mitigations successful" but keeping incident open for post-incident review. Recommend retro to cover cache eviction thresholds and routing policy heuristics.

Alex P: agreed. I'll move incident to "monitoring" state on status page and schedule a follow-up RFC for kernel selection tweaks. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:

OpsBot: INCIDENT INC-2026-042: status -> monitoring. Next update scheduled in 1h.

Jordan M: follow-ups: (1) add more aggressive cache warming for long-sequence jobs, (2) add autoreduce batch sizing on eviction detection, (3) add metric alert for memory-churn-to-latency correlation.

Alex P: assigning action items: Jordan (runtime) - PR for autoreduce batching, Sara (oncall) - add postmortem template and severity justification, Marta (CS) - collect customer impact notes. I’ll own RC and timeline.

Alex P: closing note: full recovery expected once we revert routing to normal and validate no regressions — target window today +3h for final revert after canary ramps.

Oncall Bot: INCIDENT INC-2026-042: thread archived to incidents channel with resolution state pending postmortem.
